edges.description: Failed SECISBP2-dependent Sec incorporation reduces synthesis of multiple human selenoproteins.
Reduced synthesis of deiodinase selenoproteins disrupts thyroid hormone activation and inactivation.
Deficiency of antioxidant selenoproteins increases cellular reactive oxygen species and stress sensitivity.

The route the originating report favours for the auditory deficit: reactive oxygen species injure the cochlea, and the cumulative character of that damage fits the report's observation that the older of its two probands had the more severe deficit. The report weighs a thyroid route against this one, noting that hearing loss occurs in dio2-null mice but that its patients' hormone profile fits a combined partial deficiency of all deiodinases rather than that pattern, so the edge is drawn from oxidative vulnerability and not from impaired thyroid hormone metabolism. That comparison is made in the report's discussion, which is quotable only across a line-broken word, so it is recorded here rather than as a snippet.

nodes.description: Deiodinases are selenoproteins required for thyroid hormone metabolism. Their reduced activity produces the characteristic abnormal thyroid function tests observed in SECISBP2 deficiency.

evidence.reference_title: Mutations in SECISBP2 result in abnormal thyroid hormone metabolism.
evidence.snippet: Deiodinases (DIOs) are selenoproteins involved in thyroid hormone metabolism.

nodes.description: Bilateral sensorineural hearing loss with a cochlear-level defect has been documented in SECISBP2 deficiency, more marked in the older of the two reported probands. The originating report attributes it to oxidative cochlear injury from the loss of antioxidant selenoproteins, and specifically considers and sets aside a thyroid-hormone route, so it is wired here from oxidative-stress vulnerability rather than from impaired thyroid hormone metabolism.
